meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
I know who you are, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and when?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. And what did you base it on?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing that down. He told me he wrote it over the weekend, so he pasted it in from somewhere else.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine, he'll bring it. Whatever happens with this, it stays off his record and it stays out of that classroom.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare all the time, Hale. That's a deduction, not a zero.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. So what are you proposing?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and an essay; that's the point of an outline. And you still haven't answered me.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4, in writing tonight, with the date of the rewrite in it. He'll do it to put this behind him, not because he did anything.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll confirm with him tonight. Who else will be in that room?
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed under procedure 4.4 to a private supervised rewrite for Owen, after school and not in front of his class, before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require that agreement in writing, with the date of the rewrite and the names of everyone who will be in the room. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record, still wanting your written confirmation tonight with the date and who will be present; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: showing the version history with its exact times, because it was dated, tied to his own document and something she could check on the screen herself.
What cost ground: nothing; you owned entering the zero early in one sentence and never leaned on the checker score or called Owen dishonest.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the whole essay between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM on October 28, the night before it was due, which landed very close to that night; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she asked what you were proposing after the misquote, put the 4.4 offer on the table right then instead of adding the outline, which left her outline objection unanswered.
